Vice President JD Vance faces an uphill battle to become Donald Trump’s immediate successor in the White House via victory in the 2028 election, according to influential conservative radio host and pundit Erick Erickson.

Erickson noted on his radio show how it is “very common” for vice presidents to win their political party’s nominations but “very, very, very rare” for incumbent veeps “to actually win general elections.”

That, he argued, is “part of Vance’s problem.”

“History is against him. Maybe he could defy it, but being the vice president of the United States, to this president in particular, who’s rather mercurial, very transactional, who could blow up at him at any moment, probably not the way for the Republicans to win the White House,” he continued.

Erickson warned that “there is a lot on the line for Republicans in 2028,” citing the party’s challenges in regaining control of Congress, which it lost in the 2026 midterms, and the stakes for the Supreme Court.

He raised similar doubts about Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who has also been tipped as an heir to Trump, despite acknowledging that Rubio has “some of the highest popularity ratings of this administration.”

“But can a man so tied to President Trump win the presidency in 2028?” Erickson asked. “As opposed to letting one of the governors do it, a DeSantis, a Kemp, a Youngkin, a Sarah Sanders, somebody like that? It’s going to be a problem for the Republicans.”
